beats.beat: The company sells four product categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are specialty chemicals used across industries.
It does not market its own products directly. Instead, it has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to sell through the promoter's network.
Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for roughly 59% of revenue in each of the last three financial years (FY2015–FY2017).
Exports go to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, with total exports of ₹10.68 crore over the past five years.
The company highlights its diversified product portfolio, import substitution opportunity, support from the holding company, and continuous R&D as competitive strengths.

beats.beat: The restated financials cover six periods: six months ended September 2017, and the five financial years from FY2013 to FY2017. All figures in ₹ lakh.
Profit after tax turned positive from FY2015:
PAT was ₹(27.40) lakh in FY2013, ₹(12.17) lakh in FY2014, ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017, and ₹132.75 lakh in the six months ended September 2017.
Operating cash flow has been volatile:
Net cash from operations was ₹200.97 lakh in FY2013, ₹127.73 lakh in FY2014, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2015, ₹802.59 lakh in FY2016, ₹(349.75) lakh (negative) in FY2017, and ₹124.86 lakh in H1 FY2018.
Total assets stood at ₹3,018.66 lakh as of March 2013, fluctuated, and rose to ₹3,424.96 lakh by September 2017.

Basic earnings per share (EPS) improved from negative to positive: (₹0.45) in FY2013, (₹0.20) in FY2014, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 for the six months ended September 2017.
Revenue from operations and EBITDA are not disclosed in the extracted data, so revenue trends cannot be reported here.

beats.beat: The company is controlled by four Promoters: Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (the corporate promoter).
Before the issue, Promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares — 99.76% of the paid-up capital. Promoter Group (excluding Promoters) holds the remaining 0.24%.
The company has entered into related party transactions in each of the last five years and the six months ended September 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18.

Past instances of non‑filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies have occurred, and certain licences for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9‑10, GIDC Waghodia have not yet been obtained.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at ₹1 trillion in FY2017, having grown at 10–12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017. CRISIL forecasts 12–14% CAGR going forward.
The industry is highly fragmented: small and medium enterprises hold 70–75% of the market. Only a few Indian players can compete with global giants on product innovation.

Growth drivers include rising consumption, an expanding middle class, government initiatives such as the Draft National Chemical Policy, and 100% FDI allowance. Also, stricter environmental regulations in China have reduced competition from that country.
The chemicals sector has historically been a net importer: imports grew at 6.4% CAGR vs exports at 6% CAGR over FY2013–FY2017.
Key applicable regulations include REACH for exports to the EU, GST implemented from July 2017, and environmental laws governing emissions and waste.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — functional additives and chemically modified minerals — to industrial customers. It is listing on the SME board of NSE to raise funds for a new factory and to create a public market for its shares.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising, and why it matters.

beats.beat: The company is raising funds via a fresh issue of equity shares. The proceeds are to be used for capital expenditure on a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and for general corporate purposes.
An additional objective is to list the shares on NSE EMERGE, the SME platform, to create a public trading market and enhance visibility.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited. The registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

The filing does not disclose whether there is an offer for sale (OFS) component or the identity of any selling shareholder. The price band and total issue size are also not stated in the extracted sections.

beats.beat: No long‑term customer or supplier agreements: The company does not have long‑term contracts with customers or raw‑material suppliers. It relies on purchase orders, making volumes and prices uncertain. [^drhp-p25][^drhp-p26]
Negative cash flow risk: Operating cash flow turned negative ₹(349.75) lakh in FY2017, which could strain liquidity and growth if repeated. [^drhp-p50]
Missing statutory licences: The company has not yet obtained all required licences for the manufacturing plant at Plot 9‑10, GIDC Waghodia, exposing it to potential penalties or shutdown. [^drhp-p19]
Dependence on corporate promoter for sales: The entire product distribution runs through the network of 20 Microns Limited. Any disruption in that arrangement would directly hit revenue. [^drhp-p112]
Foreign exchange exposure: The company exports to three countries and faces currency fluctuation risk, which could affect margins and cash flows. [^drhp-p21]
